source.title: Learning Implicitly Recurrent CNNs Through Parameter Sharing

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper compares parameter-sharing CNNs with standard CNNs and reports held-out classification errors, testing an architectural change’s effect on natural-data generalization. It does not test any listed version’s specific claim.
record.gate_note: The synthetic shortest-path results concern extrapolation outside the training span, which the claim excludes. The classification results report test error but not training error or the train–test gap.
record.test_reason: Table 1 compares classifiers with and without dropout, bearing on V6 in Wide ResNets and networks with soft parameter sharing. The other architectural comparisons do not test a listed version. Training error is unnecessary for testing V6's held-out-error claim.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is accurate: soft parameter sharing can reduce parameter counts while maintaining accuracy, sometimes lowers classification error, and improves synthetic-task extrapolation. The authors also emphasize emergent recurrent structures and competitive architecture-search performance. They do not claim a general dropout benefit.
record.recipe_differences: The intervention reparameterizes CNN layers as learned combinations of shared templates; it does not test the claim’s random-label memorization setup or its listed architecture, optimizer, batch-size, regularization, model-size, and gap-measure comparisons.
record.method_sensitivity: The number of templates and recurrence regularization affect the reported outcomes; CIFAR results also include models with and without dropout, and the synthetic task reports poorer adaptation to later curriculum phases with recurrence regularization.

fits_no_version.finding: Soft parameter sharing preserves or improves image-classification performance while permitting substantial parameter savings.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Learned sharing across convolutional layers can improve parameter efficiency and sometimes reduce held-out error.

record.problems: The paper reports test error but not training error, so it does not establish effects on the train–test gap. Table 1 says results average 5 runs but gives no uncertainty intervals. Some table text is flattened and does not preserve every model-value alignment.
record.rows_left_out: The synthetic shortest-path curriculum results and recurrence-regularized comparison are excluded because they concern extrapolation outside the training span, which the claim explicitly separates.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and its comparison with natural-label held-out performance.
Widening beyond a measured zero-training-error threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under matched tuning.
Batch-size effects and recipe adaptations under fixed epoch budgets.
Very small training sets, dropout-rate sweeps and underfitting, fully connected classifiers, and removing dropout together with weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its association with generalization gaps.
Removing memorized examples versus removing random examples.

missing.what: WRN 28-10* with dropout p=0.3: CIFAR-10 error 3.89 and CIFAR-100 error 18.85, versus 4.0 and 19.25 without dropout. Add dataset-specific comparisons; Table 1 reports averages over five runs without uncertainty intervals.

record.verdict_notes: The record overlooks the dropout comparisons. Table 1 is flattened, but its ordering, the stated relative improvements, and Table 2 resolve the relevant values. Width comparisons do not establish V2 because no interpolation threshold is measured. Synthetic shortest-path results bear on none of the supplied versions.

versions.untested_parts: No random-label training or comparison of random-label and natural-label test performance.
No width sweep past the zero-training-error threshold.
No comparison of convolutional and fully connected networks, sparse local connections, or convolutional initialization.
No comparison of adaptive optimizers with SGD on the claimed generalization difference.
No dropout intervention testing its effect on test error across the stated regimes.
No magnitude-aware sharpness or other generalization measure is related to the train–test gap.
No removal of memorized examples or comparison with random-example removal.

rows.operation_detail: Test error on CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 for the baseline WRN.

conditions.value: 200 epochs; SGD with Nesterov momentum 0.9; batch size 128; weight decay 5 × 10−4; augmentation

rows.subject: SWRN 28-10

conditions.value: 200 epochs; SGD with Nesterov momentum 0.9; batch size 128; weight decay 5 × 10−4; augmentation

rows.uncertainty: Results are average of 5 runs; per-result uncertainty not stated.

rows.check: This is the no-dropout SWRN comparator. Correct CIFAR-100 error to 18.78, not 18.43. Table 1's ordering and the stated 2.5% relative reduction from 19.25 support this assignment; Table 2 independently assigns 18.43 to the dropout model.

source_check.correct: No-dropout SWRN 28-10: CIFAR-10 error 3.74%; CIFAR-100 error 18.78%. WRN baselines: 4.0% and 19.25%. The recorded 18.43% belongs to SWRN 28-10 with dropout. Weight decay excludes coefficients alpha. This parameter-sharing comparison alone cannot establish a dropout effect.
source_check.locator_found: Table 1, SWRN 28-10 and SWRN 28-10* rows; Section 4.1 paragraph reporting relative reductions of 6.5% and 2.5%; Table 2 confirms the dropout values.
